findings.text: follow-on: _selene_psrc_loader reaches into a private helper, importing _widen_limiter_box from imas_ambix.worldmodel.equilibrium_labels. The widening is correctly shared rather than re-typed, but a cross-module private import couples the eval layer to a worldmodel implementation detail; if a third machine's loader needs the same derivation, promoting _widen_limiter_box (and the box type) to a small public seam would keep the coupling one-way and explicit.

follow-on: _jt60sa_xpoint_vessel_box hardcodes the OP1 store path (machine_description/OP1/wall.nc) and DD 4.1.1, and the cache key is the empty argument list, so it derives exactly one box. It is correct for the current node (the plan names OP1), but a later phase store or a second JT-60SA description would need the path/DD parameterized rather than a second hardcoded function.

follow-on: the loader's box admission is exercised with a synthetic constant X-point (_set_xpoint writes a constant calRX/calZX), so the change is proven to admit an in-range value and to null an out-of-range one, but not yet a measured PSRC X-point. A real JT-60SA X-point arrives only with the §7 read-only EDDB boundary fetch; until then the box's effect on the reference geometry is unmeasured against real data.

item_verdicts.goal: the node implements plan §7's jtmm-xpoint-vessel-box exactly as specified: xpoint_null_set and build_geometry_from_arrays take an optional box=(r_lo, r_hi, z_abs), threaded to the private _null_in_vessel, defaulting to MAST's XPOINT_VESSEL_R_RANGE=(0.1,2.0)/XPOINT_VESSEL_Z_ABS=2.0 so existing MAST callers and labels are unchanged. The SELENE reference loader (_selene_psrc_loader, imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py:163) passes JT-60SA's box, derived once from the OP1 phase store's wall limiter contour through _widen_limiter_box, widened by the margin MAST's box carries over MAST's measured extent (+0.10 m each R side, +0.17 m |Z|). Verified independently against the store: the OP1 wall.nc (DD 4.1.1) limiter contour has 51 vertices spanning R∈[1.705,4.483], |Z|≤3.0191; the derived box is (1.605,4.583,3.1891) — the same value the fragment names. No coordinate is typed by hand.

justifications.durability: meaningful asserts throughout: the in-limiter test requires the X-point slots finite and equal to (2.60, 0.0) to 1e-3, the out-of-limiter test requires them NaN, the contour test requires the derived box to bracket the real OP1 limiter (R and |Z|), and the label test requires an explicit box to keep a null MAST's default rejects. The declared negative control fires, and my independent mutation of the derivation fires it too. It is weaker where the admitted X-point is a synthetic constant rather than a real PSRC null, so the loader's box is proven to admit an in-range value but not yet a measured X-point (deferred by the plan to the §7 boundary fetch).
justifications.evidence: the gate reproduces. gate.log is '44 passed' EXIT=0 at d7ebe21b, and my independent head arm at d7ebe21b gives 44 passed EXIT=0 with imas_ambix.worldmodel.equilibrium_labels.__file__ under the scratch tree (head-arm.log). The base arm at 2c3b99bf over the same four files is 40 passed EXIT=0 (base-arm.log). The declared negative control reproduces in kind and I falsified the box check with my own mutation: forcing _jt60sa_xpoint_vessel_box to return MAST's box (0.1,2.0,2.0) in a scratch tree reddens test_loader_keeps_xpoint_inside_jt60sa_limiter and test_derived_box_contains_the_whole_op1_limiter_contour, 2 failed and 25 passed, EXIT=1 against a green head arm (review-negative-control.log). Independent real-data checks pass: the derived box equals the limiter extent widened by the computed margins, and the box contains the whole contour. One gap lowers this: admission is exercised with synthetic constant X-points (R=2.6 and 5.2 m), not a real PSRC X-point, and the reviewed record's baseline_suite/after_suite are null so it supplies no base arm (I supplied one).
justifications.fit: the change follows the module idiom: an optional keyword-only box defaulting to None→MAST, docstrings that state the mechanism (the box is coarse, the default is MAST's, the widening measures MAST's own margin), no version/plan/sprint/ticket identifier in any name, comment or docstring, and _widen_limiter_box placed beside the constants it reads. Two mild couplings, both noted as follow-ons: efit_referee imports the private _widen_limiter_box across modules, and _jt60sa_xpoint_vessel_box hardcodes the OP1 store path and DD 4.1.1.
